title: Operator Responsibility Structured Approval Modal Decision
claim: FP-MCP-280 establishes that operator responsibility is the authority model and that structured human approval evidence may be recorded through the native MCP approval modal after review; approval recording does not create clearance, consume approval, clear disable switches, contact runner start, start OpenCode, submit prompts, call wait, or run a canary.
summary: FP-MCP-280 prepares the structured human approval boundary for the FP-MCP-276 request REQ-20260704T115428653Z-fc0b6275. The operator responsibility doctrine applies: the human operator owns authorization, policy judgment, and final responsibility. GPT prepares scope and evidence; ForgePilot records and enforces boundaries; the MCP approval modal is the final brake after review. This checkpoint exists so FP-MCP-280 can serve as the approval packet before a structured approval recorder retry. A prior full structured approval invocation was platform-blocked before reaching MCP; a compact retry reached MCP but correctly failed closed because FP-MCP-280 did not yet exist and the workspace was dirty. This checkpoint does not record approval itself.
caveats: This checkpoint is not human approval evidence.
This checkpoint does not create local clearance.
This checkpoint does not consume approval.
This checkpoint does not clear the disable switch or enable execution.
This checkpoint does not contact runner start or start OpenCode.
A structured approval retry may still fail or be denied by the operator through the native MCP modal.
boundaries: human approval not recorded by this checkpoint

operatorResponsibilityDoctrine.modalRole: final brake after review, not the review itself

structuredRecord.nextStep: retry compact structured human approval from clean state before expiry if operator allows native MCP modal
